# Change ledger

What changed in the repository, newest first, added as each change goes in. Each entry says what changed, where,
and how it was checked. Experiment results stay in `research/experiments/` and the
[findings register](research/findings-register.md); this ledger records the tools and documents.

Before 5 November 2026 the history is in Git and in the experiment notes.

## 18 November 2026

### Custom walls, stage M3 (item 4): a door in a made wall's doorway breaks with it

- A door copied from one of the map's own walls into a made wall's doorway was already listed in the made wall's
  columns where its original's listing lands (`native_copy.edit_columns`, the made wall being a fracturing copy);
  now a test holds it (`DoorInMadeWall`: URB_Bar's door 7 and frame in a made wall on the pavement).
- A door that nothing lists (one brought from another map, or one that stood in no wall) is now listed too:
  [frac_walls.py](tools/bake/frac_walls.py) `door_columns` lists each door-family copy whose box meets a made wall's
  opening in the wall's columns within a tile of it along the wall, on every storey the wall reaches, each entry a
  copy of one of the map's own entries for a piece of that class (its MinZ the door's lowest point less one, as the
  game's frames save it). The game lists URB_Bar's door 7 over four tiles of its wall, both storeys.
  [native_copy.py](tools/bake/native_copy.py) calls it after `edit_columns`, logs each door listed and puts them in
  the manifest (`doorListings`); add_walls' records carry their opening boxes.
- [run_tests.py](tools/run_tests.py) reads a suite's result after unittest's "Ran N tests" line, not from the last
  five lines only: a test's prints can come after it in the log (the bake suite's Build output did).

Checked: the bake suite (`-k frac`: 44 tests; new: `DoorInMadeWall`, and `StagedDoorInMadeWall`: door 7 and its
frame brought from URB_Bar into a made wall's doorway on URB_PoliceStation, listed in all nine of the wall's columns
round the doorway, the wall reaching three of the station's storeys); the repo suite. Not seen in the game yet (run
C: a door in a made wall when the wall round it breaks).

### Custom walls, stage M2 (editor side): one-storey walls

- A made wall has a white handle on its top: dragged down past half a storey it makes the wall one storey (208 tall,
  to 192 over the floor), up past half a storey two again; the piece panel's Wall section says its height and has a
  One storey / Two storeys button. An opening the lower wall can't hold has its top brought down to 168 (24 under
  the top, as on a tall wall), and one in the upper storey goes; the drag's hint says so
  ([walls.js](tools/viewer/web/walls.js): `storeysOf`, `wallTop`, `topMostOf`, `withStoreys`, `raisedWall`;
  [app.js](tools/viewer/web/app.js), [index.html](tools/viewer/web/index.html)). Two storeys leaves the number out,
  so M1's walls keep their meshes.
- The page asks the server for a one-storey wall's own mesh (both of the page's mesh keys go through one spelling,
  `madeWallNumbers`; [generated.py](tools/viewer/generated.py) takes `storeys` 1 or 2), and the compiler passes
  `storeys` to the Build ([compiler.py](tools/editor/compiler.py): 1 or 2, else malformed).

Checked: the node suite (walls_test: heights, words, openings brought down or dropped, the top handle's half-storey
step, an opening's highest top), the viewer and editor suites' generated-wall tests (the mesh request's storeys, a
one-storey wall drawn 192 high, the compiler's storeys), `browser_smoke.py --only walls --projects` on a test server
(the top handle makes the wall one storey with its openings under its top, the mesh drawn is the one-storey one, the
button makes it two again, undo steps back through both); a close shot of the police station test wall at one storey
showed the donor's tiles to the cornice at its top.

### Custom walls, stage M2 (Build side): light that fits, one-storey walls

- A made wall's lightmap is a rectangle of its own size: [frac_wall.py](tools/bake/frac_wall.py) packs its charts at
  the donor's density on its faces (0.196 texels a unit, measured on URB_Bar's donor in a baked Build) into the
  smallest rectangle of whole DXT1 blocks it finds (`pack_rect`, `lightmapRect`; the old square left about 30% empty),
  and [frac_walls.py](tools/bake/frac_walls.py) gives the copy's lightmap that rectangle in its own cloned atlas, which
  the relight fills (`set_light`). A 16-tile wall gets 300 x 260 texels.
- The dominant light: in a baked Build each made wall gets a shadow map of its own (a clone of one of the map's
  ShadowMap2D of that light and of its texture, the lightmap's rectangle), which the relight fills as a piece of
  another map's, and the light is taken off its IrrelevantLights (the donor, an inside wall, lists the Bar's moon
  there) (`dominant_shadow`, `shadow_map_export`, `irrelevant`, `add_shadow_ref`).
- A Build without baking gives each made wall one even light (D9): every vertex at one texel of the lightmap of the
  map's nearest lit piece, the texel nearest its median light (`even_light`), and that piece's shadow map of the
  dominant light at the same texel, or the light listed irrelevant where the piece has none (`piece_shadow`). The
  Build's log says which.
- One-storey walls: a wall's numbers take `storeys` (2, as before, when left out; or 1). A one-storey wall stands
  from -16 to 192, as the game's one-storey inside walls do (URB_PoliceStation's four, URB_IndustrialOffice's): the
  donor's section with its face to 180 and its cornice from there to the top; its upper storey's slots are empty
  (`shaped`). The Build checks the number.
- [native_copy.py](tools/bake/native_copy.py) passes the bake flag to the walls and logs each wall's lightmap.

Checked: the bake suite (`-k frac`: 42 tests; new: the even light and its shadow map on the Bar, a baked Build's
layout with the relight left out (`BakedLayout`: each wall's rectangle in its own atlas, its own shadow map of the
moon, the moon off its IrrelevantLights, the relight's receivers list it), the one-storey shape, collision and box,
the face density along a wall within 1%), the viewer and editor suites' generated-wall tests; a real baked Build of a
2-, 6- and 16-tile wall beside the donor on URB_Bar: the relight wrote each lightmap rectangle and shadow map, and on
the faces the walls have 0.193, 0.196 and 0.196 texels a unit against the donor's 0.196 (the plan's check: within a
tenth). Not seen in the game yet (run B).

### Custom walls, stage M1 (editor side): the wall tool

Walls are drawn in the editor on any map (branch `fracturing-wall-poc`).

- **The Add panel's Walls kind** ([app.js](tools/viewer/web/app.js) `wallEntries`, [pieces.js](tools/viewer/web/pieces.js)
  `drawWallIcon`, [piece_categories.js](tools/viewer/web/piece_categories.js)): one entry per look, a recipe in This map
  and All maps; M1 has the Bar's inside wall ([walls.js](tools/viewer/web/walls.js) `WALL_LOOKS`). Choosing it reads the
  donor (this map's own piece on URB_Bar, else from URB_Bar through the library), then a press on the ground, a drag
  along a tile line and a release make the wall (a see-through box shows it while dragging; Shift keeps drawing, Esc
  stops). The wall is an added copy of the donor carrying `generated`, as the proof of concept's were.
- **A made wall's height is free**: the pose rule's whole storeys from the donor no longer hold it (its columns are
  made for where it stands, and the donor's height on its own map seldom matches another map's floors: the first wall
  drawn on URB_PoliceStation stood 46 into the ground). It stands on the floor under the drag's start; its tiles and
  quarter turns still follow the donor's ([compiler.py](tools/editor/compiler.py) `add`, app.js `recipeOf`).
- **Handles** on a picked made wall: white ones at its ends (whole tiles, the openings kept where they are in the
  world, one the wall no longer holds dropped), blue ones on each opening (its middle slides it, its sides in whole
  tiles or with Alt in steps of 8, its top, a window's sill). The view draws each step as the Build makes it, the last
  drawing kept until the next arrives.
- **The piece panel's Wall section** ([index.html](tools/viewer/web/index.html), [style.css](tools/viewer/web/style.css)):
  its size in words, its openings listed with what the game does at each (walked, seen through, the cover under it;
  a doorway with no door in it says so) and a Remove button, Add doorway, Add window, Flip sides, Reshuffle. Delete with
  an opening's handle last touched takes that opening out. Each change is one undo step.
- **Select all of a kind** counts a made wall as its look's mesh (its template's).
- **Fixed**: selecting a made wall threw (the panel read a vertex count the made mesh's record hasn't), which also kept
  each change to it off the undo stack.

Checked: [browser_walls.py](tools/viewer/tests/browser_walls.py) (`browser_smoke.py --only walls --projects` on a test
server: a wall drawn on URB_PoliceStation by mouse, openings, both kinds of handle, flip, undo and redo, Delete of an
opening, saved and reopened, a quick Build with the donor brought from URB_Bar and the doorway warned of); a compiler
case for the free height; the editor, viewer, node and repo suites. The game has not seen a drawn wall yet (run A).

### Custom walls, stage M1 (Build side): a made wall on any map, empty slots drawn, what an opening does in play

The custom geometry plan's stage M1, first part (branch `fracturing-wall-poc`; the plan is private, its stages are
named here by number).

- **A donor from another map** works as it is: a made wall copied from URB_Bar's inside wall onto a map without it
  is staged by the transplant like any piece of another map and made from numbers through the staged actor
  ([test_frac_walls.py](tools/bake/tests/test_frac_walls.py) `StagedDonor`: two walls on URB_PoliceStation, one turned a
  quarter so its columns run along y).
- **A slot with nothing in it** (a doorway over a whole storey's face) no longer stops the editor drawing the wall:
  [generated.py](tools/viewer/generated.py) gives such a slot one triangle of no area inside the wall, so every slot
  keeps its place for the page's materials. The Build already writes the empty section as the mesh's.
- **What an opening does in the game**, by the game's own sweeps along the lines between tiles' centres (cover 44 to
  60, high or low 88 to 104, walking 64, sight 96 over the floor; `research/native/cover-build.md`,
  `line-of-sight.md`): [compiler.py](tools/editor/compiler.py) `opening_play` and `made_wall_openings` warn of a doorway
  with no door in it (a unit in it has cover toward its sides), an opening no tile's centre line passes through, a
  doorway under the walking line, and a window walked through, giving no cover, or not seen through. A door counts
  when a door's box (a copy's, or one of the map's own left in place) overlaps the doorway.
- **The wall tool's pure part**, [walls.js](tools/viewer/web/walls.js): a drag to a wall's pose and numbers (tile edge to
  tile edge along x or y, on the tile line nearest the start, 1 to 16 tiles, the donor's z by whole storeys with no gap
  under it, quarter turns from the donor's yaw), the ends moved by whole tiles with the openings kept where they are,
  openings added in the free tile nearest the middle and moved and sized within the wall and off their neighbours,
  flip and reshuffle, and the same play rule in words for the piece panel.
- **The Window preset's size**, measured: [wall-openings.py](research/evidence/wall-openings.py) pairs the install's
  glass pieces with the walls they stand in: the game's windows run 64 to 170 over the floor, one or two tiles wide.
  Ours runs 72 to 168, so the walking line at 64 meets the wall under it as it meets the game's glass.

Checked: [walls_test.mjs](tools/viewer/tests/walls_test.mjs); `OpeningTests` in
[test_compiler_generated.py](tools/editor/tests/test_compiler_generated.py) (and the page's sweeps against the
compiler's); [test_generated.py](tools/viewer/tests/test_generated.py) (an empty slot); the staged-donor build; the
editor and node suites. The page's tool itself comes next; the game has not seen an empty section yet (run A).

### Clear map: the Skyranger stays drawn with its effects; the map's ambient sounds go; the Skyranger's dust moves with it

The user, on a cleared Bar: effect and sound markers were left in the play area, and the Skyranger's effects stayed
though the Skyranger itself was gone ("either leave the skyranger and its effects on a clear or remove both").

- **The Skyranger was never taken out; the view hid it.** The clear keeps the landing's pieces, and the Build left
  the Skyranger where it was. But the page took the kept zone for moved and hid the Skyranger and the drop zone's
  frame, drawing an outline in their place, while it still drew their lights and dust. The zone is the install's line
  joined with the map's own landing, and on the Bar that line stands a unit off the frame (719 against 719.9998). The
  page's test allowed half a unit; the Build's (native_spawns.py `unmoved`) allows 4 units for the frame and the
  soldier points. Before a clear the page has no zone list of its own, so the test never ran. The clear writes one,
  and the Skyranger vanished. [spawns.js](tools/viewer/web/spawns.js) `landingUnmoved` now follows the Build's rule,
  and [app.js](tools/viewer/web/app.js) `movedLandingActors` and `landingShifts` use it.
- **The map's ambient sounds go with a clear** ([native_copy.py](tools/bake/native_copy.py): the AmbientSound
  classes moved from `CLEAR_KEEP` to `CLEAR_OUT` and `KEEP_OUTSIDE`). They follow the emitters' rule: the
  landing's stay (the Skyranger's sound), so do those outside the play area when the tick keeps the scenery outside,
  one the project moved (the sounds lane's moves join `effect_moved`), and the project's copies (made after the
  clear). [effects_rules.js](tools/viewer/web/effects_rules.js) `survivesClear` no longer keeps every sound. Sounds
  stayed before because the clear came before sounds could be edited.
- **The Skyranger's dust moves with it** (export 35): the ARC_Skyranger_Ground_Periphery emitter stands beside the
  Skyranger's prefab, not in it. [scene_metadata.py](tools/viewer/scene_metadata.py) `landing_metadata` lists it with
  the nearest Skyranger (within 2,500 units) as role `dust`. A moved zone now carries it with the Skyranger's mesh,
  lights and sound, in the Build (native_spawns `plan`) and in the view; before, it stayed where the Skyranger had
  been. The Farm's Skyrangers have none.
- **The Clear window** (`clearedEffects`) counts the effects and ambient sounds it removes and the landing's it
  keeps: on the Bar "Removes 964 pieces, 254 lights, 9 spawn points (...), 70 effects and 5 ambient sounds. Keeps the
  landing's 2 pieces and its 3 effects and sounds, ...".
- The guide ([guide.html](tools/release/guide/guide.html)): the Clear map window's counts and what stays (the
  Skyranger's lights, dust and sound), the tick keeping sounds outside, and "Effects and ambient sounds go with the
  clear". The `clear-map` picture is retaken (its new counts; 484 by 379).
- Checked:
  - node tests: clear_map (`landingUnmoved`: the Bar's line a unit off its frame is unmoved; a tile off, or turned,
    is moved; a frameless landing by its fitted zone) and effects_rules (a sound goes, one outside stays with the
    tick, the landing's stays);
  - the viewer suite (test_spawns: the Bar's Skyranger lists its dust Emitter_0);
  - bake tests:
    - ClearLevel: the Bar's five ambient sounds go; the Skyranger's lights, dust and sound stay as the landing's;
    - BarMoved: a moved zone moves 15 actors, the dust among them;
    - Lanes: a cleared build keeps the moved sound, its copy and the Skyranger's, and takes the map's other four;
  - editor and repo suites;
  - the browser smoke `--only spawns,clear-map,effects` on a test server. After a clear no landing piece is taken for
    moved, and only the landing's effects and sounds are left. The window names the ambient sounds.
  - On the test server, a cleared Bar shows its Skyranger with its lights and dust. Not built in the game.

### Clear map deletes the map's spawn points; no-spawn volumes are edited and added; multiplayer starts hidden

The user, on a cleared Bar: the map's pods, Meld points and grey points stayed. Asked what the grey points and the
no-spawn volumes are: "If no spawn points matter then leave them in, but make them editable and allow them to be
added via the add panel".

- **Clear map** ([app.js](tools/viewer/web/app.js) `clearedSpawns`, `clearMap`): deletes the map's pods, Meld points
  and drop-in points in the clear's one undo step, but one something names (the Build would keep it and warn: it
  stays, with its edit, and the window names it), and takes away the project's copies of them. No-spawn volumes and
  the mission streams' objects stay. The window counts the spawn points it removes and the volumes it keeps; its
  plain Enemy Within note now says to place pods with the Add panel. A pod or Meld point copied from a deleted one
  builds: [native_spawns.py](tools/bake/native_spawns.py) no longer refuses a copy whose template the same edit
  deletes (the template stays in the package, off the level's list).
- **Deleted points hidden** ([spawns_view.js](tools/viewer/web/spawns_view.js) `shownEntries`): a base point the
  project deletes is drawn only with the Spawns flyout's new **Deleted points** switch (off at first), pale, to be
  restored ([index.html](tools/viewer/web/index.html)).
- **Multiplayer teams' starts** (XComSpawnPoint unit types 8 and 9, the Bar's twelve grey points) get no marker:
  single player never uses them, and Long War's landing mutator logs them as bad spawn points.
- **No-spawn volumes edited** (export 34, [scene_metadata.py](tools/viewer/scene_metadata.py) `SPAWN_VALUES`: their
  `aliens` and `civilians` switches, AlienNoSpawnZone and CivilianNoSpawnZone, both on in the class default):
  - the Spawns view draws each as a grey box round its marker; picked, its arrows move it by whole tiles and levels
    and the Buildings view's six white face handles move a side to tile lines and levels (Alt: steps of 8), each one
    undo step; Copy (Ctrl+D, a tile east, its size), Delete, Restore, and two ticks, Keeps aliens out and Keeps
    civilians out;
  - the Add panel's **Spawn points** has **No-spawn volume** on every map: a copy of the map's first volume, its size,
    over whole tiles round the click, or on a map with none a new 3 by 3 tile, four-level volume
    ([pieces.js](tools/viewer/web/pieces.js) draws its icon);
  - the project's records ([project.js](tools/viewer/web/project.js)): an override with `box` [x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1]
    and/or `spawn`, never a pose; an added `kind: "noSpawn"` record with `box`, `from` its template or none;
  - [compiler.py](tools/editor/compiler.py): `noSpawn` among `SPAWN_EDIT_KINDS` and `SPAWN_COPY_KINDS`
    (`spawn_box`, `volume_add`); a pose on a volume, a box on a point, an empty box or a value of another kind is
    refused; the lane's move of a volume carries its `box`;
  - the writer: a volume's move sets its Location and DrawScale3D (unturned) so its brush spans the box; a copy is the
    template cloned over its box, and a new one the map's first plain no-spawn volume or, on a map with none, the

    `add_rebuild_volume` is now one of its uses); `verify` reads back each volume's scale.
- Placing a new spawn point from the Add panel lets go of the picked one, whose arrows had taken the click.
- **Pods lose Turn left and Turn right** (the user: "pods aren't aimed at anything", then "can we just get rid of
  those facing buttons ?"). Their titles said they set "the way its aliens face when they deploy", but the game's
  script (XComAlienPod.GetDistributedLocationAround) puts the first alien on the pod's place and the rest evenly

current. This merge brings in 68 commits (release 0.5.3, effects and sounds, the spawn points, the project manager's
work).

### Hidden game runs: loads of a battle with aliens no longer crash (T-46); a crash log

- [hidden_game.py](tools/lab/hidden_game.py) `dxvk_config`: every run gives DXVK its own `<out>\dxvk.conf`
  (`DXVK_CONFIG_FILE`) with `d3d9.textureMemory = 0`. With DXVK's texture budget on, every load of a save with aliens
  in the battle crashed on a thread of the game's own reading memory that was gone, Long War's reload of EXALT's
  missions among them ([findings register](research/findings-register.md) T-46: not the mouse, as first thought).
- [StandInInput.c](tools/lab/StandInInput.c), [build_stand_in_input.py](tools/lab/build_stand_in_input.py),
  hidden_game.py `--crash-log`: the stand-in DLL stands beside the game in any case and, with
  `XCOM_STAND_IN_CRASH_LOG=1`, logs the run's first faults to `<out>\input.log` (thread, code, module and offset,
  what it touched, registers, the module addresses on that thread's stack); the run prints them at its end.
- [game-test skill](.claude/skills/game-test/SKILL.md): a run that ends by itself with nothing in the log gets a rerun
  with `--crash-log`.
- Checked: [test_hidden_game.py](tools/lab/tests/test_hidden_game.py) (the settings file, the crash log's plan, a fault
  on a thread of its own named by the built DLL in [StandInInputCheck.cs](tools/lab/tests/StandInInputCheck.cs)), the
  lab suite; in the game, [EXP-72](research/experiments/EXP-72-spawns.md) runs 15 and 16: a Bar quicksave with aliens
  loaded twice with the setting, after six crashes of six without it. Known gap: with the budget off a long session
  could run out of the game's 32-bit address space (not seen).

### Hidden game runs: a stand-in mouse and keyboard when Windows has none (T-45)

- [StandInInput.c](tools/lab/StandInInput.c): a 32-bit `dinput8.dll` that hands every call to Windows' own and gives
  the game a still mouse or keyboard where Windows has none (the game's start asks DirectInput for the system mouse
  and crashed without one). No C runtime and no Windows SDK; [build_stand_in_input.py](tools/lab/build_stand_in_input.py)
  builds it with clang-cl, lld-link and llvm-dlltool (`--llvm <LLVM bin folder>`) into `<lab>\bin`, where
  [hidden_game.py](tools/lab/hidden_game.py) takes it from, as it takes DXVK from `<lab>\dxvk`.
- [hidden_game.py](tools/lab/hidden_game.py) `input_plan`: with a mouse or keyboard missing in Windows the DLL goes
  beside the game for the run and comes out after (a different `dinput8.dll` already there stops the run); the DLL
  writes what the game asked for and got to `<out>\input.log`. Without the DLL, no mouse still stops the run.
  `--stand-in-input` gives the stand-ins anyway, to check them. The
  [game-test skill](.claude/skills/game-test/SKILL.md) and the [findings register](research/findings-register.md)'s
  T-45 say so.
- Checked: [test_hidden_game.py](tools/lab/tests/test_hidden_game.py) (the plan's cases, the DLL placed and taken
  away, the built DLL in a 32-bit process by [StandInInputCheck.cs](tools/lab/tests/StandInInputCheck.cs): both
  stand-ins and every call the game makes on them), the lab suite; in the game with the stand-ins forced, URB_Bar
  started to turn 1, a soldier walked two tiles by `goto` and Escape opened the pause menu, and nothing was left
  beside the game. A start with the devices really gone hasn't been played.

### Spawns, stage SP7: the base map's pods and Meld points copied, its spawn points deleted

- **The page** ([app.js](tools/viewer/web/app.js), [spawns_view.js](tools/viewer/web/spawns_view.js)): where the
  spawn family builds, a picked base pod, Meld point or drop-in point has Copy (Ctrl+D) and Delete (Delete) in its
  panel, and [ and ] turn a pod or a drop-in point. A copy is made only from a plain pod (no commander or secondary
  flag, no forced type, no link to another actor) or any Meld point; the button says why where it can't. It lands a
  tile east with its template's values and turn, picked, and is moved, turned and given values as the map's points
  are, its marker and panel its own ("Pod: a copy of …"; its template's saved values marked "(its template's)",
  [spawn_rules.js](tools/viewer/web/spawn_rules.js)). A deleted point is drawn pale, its panel says whether the Build
  takes it out or keeps it (something names it), and Restore brings it back. Undo, Reset all, recovery and the
  header's count take them.
- **The document**: a copy is an `added[]` record of `kind` pod or meld with `from` its template, a pose and
  `spawn`; a delete is a deleted override ([project.js](tools/viewer/web/project.js) `validAdded`). One the page
  doesn't take is carried and saved back unchanged.
- **The compiler** ([compiler.py](tools/editor/compiler.py)): `spawn_add` refuses a template that isn't plain
  (`spawn-copy-template`), one of another kind, one the export lacks, and the family off; gives each pod copy the next
  pod index above every one the map's pods and its streams' save and every pod event the export's uses name
  (`free_pod_index`; across the install's maps an event names index 1 at most, a pod 53). `spawn_delete` builds a
  delete only when nothing names the point (`spawn_names`: the Kismet, a wave place, a pod event for its index, a typed
  reference, a name list) and its uses were read; else warning `spawn-delete-named`, and the point stays. SP5's place
  counts read the copies, the deletes and the SP6 values.
- **The writer** ([native_spawns.py](tools/bake/native_spawns.py)): a copy is its template cloned with its components
  (`native_copy.clone_actor`), placed, given its PodIndex (refused where a pod event of the map names it) and its
  values; a delete leaves its slot in the level's list empty. `verify` reads back each copy listed at its pose with its
  index and values, its template byte for byte as it was, and each delete off the list
  ([native_copy.py](tools/bake/native_copy.py) hands it the map before the edit).
- **Example** [exp72_sp7_project.py](tools/editor/examples/exp72_sp7_project.py): URB_Bar's pods 2 and 3 copied onto
  free floor tiles near them, Meld point 2 copied and made hard, pod 4 deleted (six pods where there were five).
- **Checked** offline on URB_Bar: built twice byte for byte the same; read back with the exporter's own spawn reader:
  the copies listed as XComAlienPod_Abduction_5 and _6 with pod indices 5 and 6 and the Meld copy hard, each with
  its template's archetype and its own clones of the template's three components; pod 4 off the list; every other
  point at its place. Tests: compiler (copies, the index above a stream's pod, deletes kept back by an event or the
  Kismet, the refusals), bake (`test_native_spawns.py`: copies and a delete written and read back, the refusals),
  build (copies and deletes in a spawn-only build), node (the copy and delete rules, `validAdded`); the page tried on
  a test server with the family on (the project's copies and delete opened as saved; copy, move, value, delete,
  restore and the keys, undone back to saved; saved from the page and compiled as the page showed it).
- **Gaps**: no paste of a copied point elsewhere (a copy lands a tile east and is dragged from there); copies of
  drop-in points and of pods with links aren't made. The game check is still to come.

### Spawns, stage SP6: the base map's pods, Meld points and drop-in points moved, turned and given values

- **The family** `spawn` ([compiler.py](tools/editor/compiler.py) `FAMILIES`): off until its game check passes (a
  test server's `--family spawn` turns it on).
- **The page** ([app.js](tools/viewer/web/app.js), [spawns_view.js](tools/viewer/web/spawns_view.js),
  [index.html](tools/viewer/web/index.html), [style.css](tools/viewer/web/style.css)): where the family builds, a
  picked base pod, Meld point or drop-in point gets the Spawns view's arrows (whole tiles across, whole levels up,
  alone), Turn left and Turn right (a quarter; the picked pod or drop-in point shows the way it faces), and its
  values: a pod's Commander's place, Secondary and Use ticks, a Meld point's Difficulty, Destroyed on turn and Spawn
  group. A value back at the map's, or a point back where and as the map has it, is no edit; "As the map has it" puts
  it back. Each change is one undo step; Reset all, recovery and the header's count ("4 spawn point edits") take
  them. The panel names the project's values "(the project's)" ([spawn_rules.js](tools/viewer/web/spawn_rules.js))
  and says what the move keeps: its name, so what uses it still does; its links stay where the map has them.
- **The document**: `overrides[]` of `target {package, level: "base", actor}` with a whole pose (only where it moved
  or turned) and `spawn`, the sparse values; [project.js](tools/viewer/web/project.js) `validOverride` takes them,
  and a record the page doesn't take (a delete, another kind's key) is carried and saved back unchanged.
- **The compiler**: `spawn_of`, `spawn_values` and `spawn_override`: refuses a kind it only shows
  (`spawn-view-only`), an actor the level doesn't list (`spawn-unlisted`), one whose values weren't read
  (`spawn-unread`), another kind's or an out-of-range value (`spawn-values`), and a delete (`spawn-delete`, SP7's);
  notes a value of no kind (carried), a point as the map has it, and the links that stay (`spawn-links`); the moves and
  values go to the native edit's `spawns` lane; SP5's place counts read the moved places; the report counts
  `spawns {moved, valued, added, deleted}`.

  [native_copy.py](tools/bake/native_copy.py)): each point edited in place under its own name (a based one's
  relative place from its base's final place), each value written as a tagged property (a flag the pod saves none of
  grows its export; the Meld difficulty as its `EMeldContainerDifficulty` name), read back after the write.
- **The Build** ([build.py](tools/editor/build.py)): spawn edits are work of their own, with no relight and the
  lighting kept; the manifest counts them (`spawnEdits`).
- **Example** [exp72_sp6_project.py](tools/editor/examples/exp72_sp6_project.py): URB_Bar's pod 0 moved a tile and
  turned a quarter, pod 1 the commander's, Meld point 2 hard and destroyed on turn 6, Meld point 3 in spawn group 1;
  `--again` builds twice, `--cleared` and `--grid` on the cleared and the resized Bar.
- **Checked** offline on URB_Bar: built twice byte for byte the same; read back with the package reader on its own:
  the same 32 actors, export indices, names and children, every point the edit didn't touch byte for byte, each
  edited point as asked; the cleared and the resized Bar build and read back the same way. Tests: compiler (the
  family off, the lane, each refusal), bake (`test_native_spawns.py`: the value bytes; Bar edited, read back, the
  rest as it was, the refusals), build (a spawn-only project in both kinds of build), node (`spawns_view_test.mjs`:
  the edit rules, the override, a saved record read back; `project_spawns_test.mjs`: `validOverride`), the families

### Effects drawn closer to the game: fires look like fire, the night smoke is no longer pink (export 31)

- [effects_draw.py](tools/viewer/effects_draw.py), draw version 4 ([export.py](tools/viewer/export.py) export 31):
  - Each particle texture's traits come from its pixels (`texture_traits`): grey, an alpha that holds a shape, packed
    channels, red share, brightness. Packed means no blue with red and green unrelated, or mostly blue to pink, as the
    night smoke's `T_Roiling_Smoke_SubUV`, whose red, green and blue are its light from below, from above and its
    density.
  - The colour and the shape come from different textures (`pick_textures`: `picture`, `opacity` alpha, brightness
    or none, `mask`, `maskFrom` brightness, alpha or red). The fires' colour is their Flame picture and their shape a
    grey mask; before, names alone gave the debris the packed smoke noise and the Flame's near-empty alpha hid them.
  - A material's own colour parameters are read (`material_colours` into `colours`) and tint a see-through particle
    with no picture. The night smoke plume's are all but black.
- [effects_sim.js](tools/viewer/web/effects_sim.js):
  - Colour channels that carry data are drawn as the mean of the others (`dataChannels`). The fires' green and blue
    offsets reach 50, and the night smoke's green is scaled by up to 200 over its life (a colour scale that differs
    by channel).
  - An alpha that rises above 1.2 erodes the shape rather than making it solid (`alphaErodes`: the fire chunks).
  - A colour saved with only a vector, as URB_Bar's webbing's, is read as that vector, not white.
- [effects_preview.js](tools/viewer/web/effects_preview.js):
  - See-through and added particles are blended premultiplied, as the game lays a bright colour at a low opacity.
  - A sprite is never thinner than two pixels (`viewHeight`).
  - A solid mesh with no colour of its own is drawn charred.
  - A dark see-through colour is lifted to a dull grey: the bar's steam is a faint wisp, not black.
  - `materialTint` gives the material's tint.
  - `describe()` gives the page's `likenessOf` hook for checks.
- [app.js](tools/viewer/web/app.js):
  - The Add panel's pane shows the row's tip inside itself; the browser's own tooltip no longer covers the drawing.
  - Pictures and the pane frame the size-weighted bulk of the particles.
  - A vector read by a colour module is labelled r, g, b, not x, y, z.
- [effects_rules.js](tools/viewer/web/effects_rules.js): a vector parameter named Color, Colour or Tint is shown and
  edited as a colour and a strength (`colourNamed`), such as `P_Power_Core_Persistent`'s Color, which scales its
  colour over life.
- [library.js](tools/viewer/web/library.js): picture version 2, so the Add panel's effect pictures are drawn again.
- [editor-contracts.md](research/editor-contracts.md): the draw record's version 4 fields.

### Effects drawn as they look: the likeness in the view (effects and sounds plan, stage FXV2)

- [effects_sim.js](tools/viewer/web/effects_sim.js), new, no three.js: one emitter stepped from its draw data. `sample`
  reads a distribution at a time (a table's entry blended to the next, a random range with its locked axes, a particle
  parameter through its mode's ranges); `makeEmitter` spawns by the rate and the bursts, gives each particle its life,
  place (a point, a box, a sphere, a cylinder), speed, size, colour, turn and sub-image, and changes them over its
  life by the followed modules; seeded, so the same effect draws the same; `LIMITS` (400 particles an emitter, 1,500
  an effect, 30,000 in the view).
- [effects_preview.js](tools/viewer/web/effects_preview.js), new: `makeLikeness` draws a system: each sprite emitter
  as instanced quads that face the camera (or lie along their speed), each mesh emitter as an instanced mesh, both
  through one shader with the picture and mask the export picked, blended as the material says (see-through, added,
  multiplied, solid). It starts warm (run ahead by its longest life) and a system that has played out starts again
  after two seconds.
- [app.js](tools/viewer/web/app.js): a likeness for every effect the Build will have (`refreshLikenesses`: the
  markers' own rule, without their filters), in every view, never picked; one that starts off only while it is
  picked; made anew when its parameters change; put where its effect stands each frame, so a drag and a size edit
  show at once; stepped only when in the picture and more than a few pixels of it (`stepLikenesses`), thinned evenly
  over the view's budget. **View options: Effects as they look**, kept in the browser. The effect panel says what the
  drawing leaves out ("Drawn here without its swirl"). An effect of another map brings its textures and meshes with
  its template.
- [effects_draw.py](tools/viewer/effects_draw.py), draw version 3: a mesh emitter carries its own textures and takes
  its blend from the material it is drawn with; a texture of three packed channels gives one channel as the opacity
  and no colour (`opacity: channel`); an emitter whose material only bends the light is not drawn.
- **From the game's own pictures** (a hidden game on URB_Bar, game-test skill): a number saved where the system reads
  a vector (and the other way) is not found by the game, which plays the distribution's constant. Bar's steam saves
  Brightness 0.05 as a number and is a dull grey wisp, not near black. `sample` does the same. This is what EXP-70
  could not judge. (**Wrong, and put right the same day**: EXP-70 run 2 showed the game reads such a number; see
  the entry on EXP-70 passing.)
- [tools/viewer/README.md](tools/viewer/README.md), [editor-contracts.md](research/editor-contracts.md) section 8.

### What an effect's likeness is drawn from: export 29 (effects and sounds plan, stage FXV1)

- [effects_draw.py](tools/viewer/effects_draw.py), new: for each emitter of a particle system (its first level of

  table or as the particle parameter that feeds it; `draw: null` with `why` for what can't be drawn (a ribbon, no level

  its archetypes in the map, the class default in the script packages and its own chain). Effects metadata version 2.

  textures go through `Exporter.texture` and a mesh particle's mesh and materials through the new `particle_mesh`,

### hidden_game.py plays turns: sessions, goto, aim

- [tools/lab/hidden_game.py](tools/lab/hidden_game.py): `--serve <idle seconds>` keeps the hidden game running and
  `send <folder> <steps>` hands it more steps and prints what the game's log answered, so a step can go by an earlier
  one's answer; `goto <folder> <x> <y>` walks the active soldier to a tile and `aim <folder> <x> <y> [steps]` puts the
  game's 3D cursor on one (the camera's field of view and yaw put the picture's corner, where the game's mouse stands,
  over the tile; the cursor is read back and corrected); `--squad <file>` lands a squad of records (the game's own
  can't walk).
- [tools/lab/GameRemote.cs](tools/lab/GameRemote.cs): steps `serve` and `quit`; a console step takes several commands
  (` | ` between them, run in one frame) and its files have short names (`xmwh<N>.txt`), which type faster.
- Checked: the `lab` suite (14 tests: the aim's camera against the four yaws measured in the game, the log answers),
  and two sessions in the lab copy on URB_Bar: a soldier walked to two tiles, a Sectoid dropped on a chosen tile was
  shot dead, another killed by a grenade aimed the same way, the turn ended and turn 2 began, cover values read back.
  Findings in [T-43](research/findings-register.md). Gaps: upper floors and roofs, saves, the LWR install not tried;
  a grenade's aim is set with the camera commands by hand.

### Game checks nobody watches: hidden_game.py

  (`--map`, Play in game's commands) or with a commands file, or stops at the main menu, and afterwards takes the DLL
  out and puts back every config file the run changed. Shots, the game's log and the run's own log go to

  wait for a log line, a console command through a typed `exec`, a typed command, a key, the game's own `shot` saved
  as a PNG). No mouse steps: the game takes no mouse there (T-43).

  checks the steps, the DXVK pick and what is put in and back, on a made-up game folder.
- Checked: the `lab` suite (9 tests), and three runs in the lab copy (the main menu by arrow keys; a battle on URB_Bar
  with console commands, Tab and camera keys; the lab copy as it was after each). Findings in
  [T-43](research/findings-register.md). Gaps: no mouse, so no soldier is moved by pointing; a played turn, saves and
  the LWR install not tried.

### Effects' and sounds' values in the compiler and the Build (effects and sounds plan, stage FX5, part 1)

- An effect's size, starting state and particle parameters, and a sound's radii, volume, pitch and starting state,
  are checked by the compiler and written by the Build, behind two gates of their own: the families `effect-values`
  and `sound-values` ([compiler.py](tools/editor/compiler.py) `FAMILIES`), off until their game check, so moves,
  copies and deletes go on building as they do (`--family effect-values` lifts one for an experiment's build). The
  page doesn't offer them yet.
- The compiler (`effect_values`, `effect_parameters`, `effect_value_warnings`): a value-only override, a move with
  values and a copy with values reach the lanes' `values` (originals, in place) and each copy's `values`, as the
  writer takes them: a parameter keeps the type its effect saves it in (a scalar saved where the system's
  distribution is a vector stays a scalar), a name it doesn't save gets the distribution's kind; refused: values
  where the export's `can.values` says no (a shared cue's), a random or untyped parameter, a name the system reads as
  both kinds or lacks, a malformed value or one outside what a value may be (`EFFECT_SCALE`, `SOUND_RADIUS_MAX`,
  `SOUND_VOLUME_MAX`, `SOUND_PITCH`, `PARAMETER_MAX`), an inner radius beyond the outer one; warned of: one set to
  start off with nothing in the script to switch it on, a starting state the script switches anyway, parameters the
  script sets too. Deletion wins over values. The report counts `valued`.
- The Build ([native_effects.py](tools/bake/native_effects.py) `set_values`, `set_parameters`, `read_values`,
  `check_values`): on the actor's own exports only (never a clone's source, an archetype or a cue asset): the
  actor's `DrawScale` multiplied (its `DrawScale3D` kept), the component's `bAutoActivate`, its `InstanceParameters`
  patched by name (an entry's value field set in place, a new name added at the end, every other entry byte for
  byte, an array added where the component saves none), a sound's node `RadiusMin`, `RadiusMax`, `VolumeMin`,
  `VolumeMax`, `PitchMin`, `PitchMax` and its actor's `bAutoPlay`; read back in the lane's verify. The native edit,
  `native_split` and the Build's dispatch carry the `values` lane ([compiler.py](tools/editor/compiler.py),
  [build.py](tools/editor/build.py), [native_copy.py](tools/bake/native_copy.py)).
- Contract: the effects' and sounds' override row ([editor-contracts.md](research/editor-contracts.md)).

Checked: [test_compiler_effects.py](tools/editor/tests/test_compiler_effects.py) `Values` (the gates, value-only and
mixed records, copies, a foreign copy against its donor's system, every refusal and warning);
[test_native_effects.py](tools/bake/tests/test_native_effects.py) `ValueLanes` on the install's URB_Bar (Emitter_38's
size, starting state, a scalar on a vector distribution, a colour and a new parameter; a value it has already leaves
the component's bytes as they were; a copy's values on the copy alone, its source and the other copy as the map has
them; a simple sound's values in place and a copy's one radius; export 28 reads them all back); test_families; the
editor, viewer and bake effect, transplant and copy suites. Known gaps: no game check yet (EXP-E), no page controls.

### Effects and sounds from other maps (effects and sounds plan, stage FX4)

The Add panel's All maps lists the base maps' effects and ambient sounds, and one placed from there is brought into
the map by the Build, as a piece of another map is.
- **The library** ([library.py](tools/viewer/library.py), index 9; [effects_library.py](tools/viewer/effects_library.py),
  new): each base map's effects and sounds are scanned with its pieces (`scan_effects`, through
  [effects_metadata.py](tools/viewer/effects_metadata.py)'s `describe`) into entries of family `effect` or `sound`,
  one per recipe (an effect's class, system, saved parameters, scale, component offset, starting state; a sound's
  class, cue, waves, values, starting state), from the map whose copy brings least, with the panel's kind (from the
  system's or wave's name). A stream's are not scanned; a landing's, one riding on another and one playing nothing
  are listed `unavailable` with why; the TextureMovie system's closure is refused as before. `library.effect` gives
  one as a template (its export 28 record, its system or waves), the donor described once into
  `effects-v1.json` in its pieces folder; the precache skips them. The full scan of 151 maps took 29 s and has 1,826
  effect and sound entries (1,671 effects, 155 sounds; 40 can't be placed).
- **The server** ([viewer.py](tools/viewer/viewer.py)): `GET /library/effect.json`, `POST /library/effects.json` (a
  project's opening) and `GET`/`HEAD /library/wave.ogg?package=&id=` (the Wave preview of another map's sound, through
  the same WaveCache). The build summary ([builds.py](tools/viewer/builds.py)) says `foreignEffects` and each donor's
  `effects`.
- **The page**: All maps' rows for them ([library.js](tools/viewer/web/library.js): the Effects view's marker as the
  picture, what each plays, where it is placed, Starts off, Not brought), the Kind menu's Effects and Sounds with their
  kinds ([piece_categories.js](tools/viewer/web/piece_categories.js)); placing one reads its template and places a copy
  as Ctrl+V does ([app.js](tools/viewer/web/app.js) `chooseLibraryEffect`, `effectTemplate`), its system and waves
  joined to the map's; a project's copies of them read back on opening (`loadForeignTemplates`); the panel says where
  one comes from; the Wave preview plays another map's wave from that map; the Build window's step counts them.
  [effects_view.js](tools/viewer/web/effects_view.js) `drawEffectIcon` draws a row's picture.
- **The compiler** ([compiler.py](tools/editor/compiler.py) `foreign_effect`, `Library.effect`): an added effect or
  sound whose `from` names another base map is checked against the library (the file it was scanned from, an entry
  of its family; `unavailable` and `closure` refused) and goes to its lane with its `donor`; the report's `donors`
  list it.
- **The Build** ([transplant.py](tools/bake/transplant.py) `stage_edit`, [build.py](tools/editor/build.py),
  [native_effects.py](tools/bake/native_effects.py)): the lanes' copies with a donor are staged in the map (each donor
  actor once, outside the level's list; a system or wave the map has by path is the map's own), the copies rewritten
  to clone the staged actor (`lane_actor` takes a staged source only outside the list); an effects-only full build
  reads the staged map too. The manifest says `foreignEffects`.
- **[F-121](research/findings-register.md), fixed:** the transplanter kept each donor's imports by `id(donor)`, which a
  later donor could take once an earlier one was freed: one build of EXP-69 staged URB_Boulevard's fountain with
  another map's class for its node. They are kept by the donor's file now ([transplant.py](tools/bake/transplant.py)
  `Destination.import_of`); any build bringing from three or more maps could meet it before.
- Docs: contract section 8's From other maps and the added-records row ([editor-contracts.md](research/editor-contracts.md)),
  [tools/viewer/README.md](tools/viewer/README.md)'s From other maps.
- Foreign effects and sounds wait for their game check (EXP-69): the compiler's `FOREIGN_FAMILIES` doesn't list
  them, so the library marks them as a kind not brought before (listed with Can be placed unticked) and the Build
  makes them as any copy. The run is prepared: [EXP-69](research/experiments/EXP-69-effects-and-sounds-from-other-maps.md)
  (URB_Bar, seven copies from six maps), its project [exp69_project.py](tools/editor/examples/exp69_project.py) and
  its marked shots ([EXP-69-shots.json](research/experiments/EXP-69-shots.json)).

Checked: [test_effects_library.py](tools/viewer/tests/test_effects_library.py) (new: recipes, kinds, what blocks);
[test_library.py](tools/viewer/tests/test_library.py) (effect entries in the index, the gate and its lift, the two-map
scan's effects and sounds, the templates, the routes and a donor wave played); test_compiler_effects (copies of other

[test_native_effects.py](tools/bake/tests/test_native_effects.py) ForeignLanes (the plan's 17 November offline trial
made a test: URB_PierA's lit sea foam and air conditioner staged in URB_Bar and cloned, two copies from one staged

### Effects and sounds, stage FX2: the Wave preview

The second stage of the effects and sounds plan, on branch `effects-and-sounds`: a picked sound's waves can be heard
in the Effects view. Nothing a Build makes changes, and the export stays at 28.
- [audio.py](tools/viewer/audio.py), new: a wave's Ogg Vorbis stream read from its PC bulk record
  ([effects_metadata.py](tools/viewer/effects_metadata.py)'s new `pc_sound`, which `wave_record` now uses too) and
  checked before it is served: one logical stream, each page's capture pattern, version, checksum and number, the
  continued-packet flags against the lacing, the identification header alone on the first page, the comment and setup
  headers before the first audio page, the end flag on the last page, granules that never go back, at most 32 MB and an
  hour. A bounded cache (64 MB) keeps each wave read; the map's own package is used only while it is the file the map
  was exported from (its SHA-256), a stream's by its size and time.
- [viewer.py](tools/viewer/viewer.py): `GET`/`HEAD /maps/<id>/wave.ogg?id=<soundWaves key>`, `audio/ogg` with its
  length, an ETag (`If-None-Match`: 304) and one byte range at a time (206; 416 outside it). An id the export doesn't
  list (a stale or made-up one, a path) is 404, a wave it can't serve 422 with why; one bad wave never fails the map.
- The effect panel's **Wave preview** ([app.js](tools/viewer/web/app.js), [index.html](tools/viewer/web/index.html),
  [style.css](tools/viewer/web/style.css)): each wave of a picked sound with Play/Stop, one at a time, at volume 0.6,
  the clock while it plays; picking something else, Escape, leaving the view or opening another map or project stops
  and releases it; a refusal shows the server's reason, a decode failure says so.
- Docs: [tools/viewer/README.md](tools/viewer/README.md) and section 8 of
  [editor-contracts.md](research/editor-contracts.md).

Checked: [test_audio.py](tools/viewer/tests/test_audio.py), new (made-up Ogg streams: a good one, one with a packet
over a page boundary, and each of 25 refusals; Ogg's CRC check value; byte ranges; the cache's refusals; on the
install, Bar's Skyranger idle wave against its own properties, the cache and its bound, and the route: GET, HEAD,
ranges, 416, 304, 404 and 422); the effects metadata tests; a sweep of every SoundNodeWave in the 97 LWR map packages
(7,192, all pass, about 0.2 s for the largest, 2.3 MB); in the browser on a test server, Play decoded Bar's
DropshipIdle at its 12.75 s, a seek went by byte range (206), Stop, the end, Escape, picking another sound, leaving

### Effects census, version 2: copies left out, the plan's evidence gaps closed

The effects and sounds plan was checked again, at the user's ask, against the code as it stands and the packages.

- **The first census counted a copy.** A variant of one map installed in the game, and its landing intro, were
  counted as Firaxis's: a map the editor builds keeps the package GUID of the map it grew from.
  [audit_effects.py](tools/upk/audit_effects.py) now counts only the oldest file of a GUID (`copies`,
  `copiesLeftOut`).
- **What it reads besides** (its docstring has the list):
  - which actors the level's actor list holds;
  - everything under each particle system, over all LOD levels, with its native bytes by class;
  - the parameters a system offers against the ones its effects save;
  - whether a system's emitters loop;
  - each wave's bulk records by their headers;
  - why a sound reaches no wave, and what its node saves or inherits;
  - each building floor's emitter list against where the emitters stand;
  - what a `Base` resolves to;
  - what the two carrying rules would pick;
  - whether LWR's patches name an effect as text;
  - `Engine.upk`'s class defaults for starting on;
  - the map list's and each package's SHA-256.
- **Its result:** [effects-audit-2026-11-17.json](research/evidence/effects-audit-2026-11-17.json), for 96 base
  maps, 54 Firaxis streams and 87 LWR patches.
  - 7,138 effects in 95 base maps and 421 in streams, every one in its level's list; 849 sounds in 90 base maps;
    92 flares.
  - Nothing under any of the 441 particle systems keeps native data. Two system paths have two sizes across
    packages; the 64 waves have one each.
  - All 64 waves keep their Ogg stream as one plain bulk record, and `RawPCMDataSize` is frames times channels
    times two on each.
  - Eight sounds play nothing: an empty sound slot, or none.
  - No ground floor lists an effect; of the 679 listings on upper floors, 471 stand inside their floor's volumes.
  - Of 17,622 saved instance parameters, 80% name one their system offers in its kind and 18% in the other kind.
  - The transplant's dry run: 7,558 of 7,559 effects, all 864 sounds and all 92 flares could come.
  - The first census's file, [effects-audit-2026-11-15.json](research/evidence/effects-audit-2026-11-15.json), is
    kept as it was made.
- **Tried offline, in a scratch folder:** `transplant.stage_edit` staged a lit effect and a simple sound of one
  map into a copy of another, and `native_copy.clone_actor` cloned both and two of the map's own. Read back, each
  clone has its own component, light environment, cue and node, with the system and the wave shared. Nothing was
  played, and the trial is not kept as a test: the plan makes it stage FX4's first.

mission the variant has no record for lost the map. A mission that asks for its map by name then found none: a
variant of Commercial Alley Redux for covert extraction only left a new campaign's first mission without a map.

  records for, from `recordMissions`) and `kept` (the missions of the others); a rotation install keeps `standsFor`
  in its ledger entry, and `replaced_records` / `_sync_off` comment out only those. An entry written before still
  replaces every record of its base map. `mission_warnings` names, under Replace, the missions left to the original
  and says when the original plays the first mission.

- The [README](tools/viewer/README.md), the [guide](tools/release/guide/guide.html) and

### The editor draws a fracturing wall made from numbers as the Build makes it

The user could not see the custom wall's doorway in the editor: a made wall was drawn as the wall it copies, so the
custom wall showed as a whole bar wall overlapping the twin, with no gap to put a door in. Now it is drawn from its
own mesh.
- [generated.py](tools/viewer/generated.py) (new): `GET /generated/fracwall.glb?wall=<its numbers as JSON>`
  ([viewer.py](tools/viewer/viewer.py)) answers the mesh [frac_wall.py](tools/bake/frac_wall.py) builds from the
  numbers, written as the export's mesh files are (`mesh.write_glb`), its six sections in slot order. The geometry
  is the numbers' and the recipe's alone, so no map is read; the last 32 are kept by their numbers. Numbers it can't
  draw (under 40 or over 3,072 long, more than 16 openings, an opening outside the wall) are refused.

  entry of its own that points there, with its box and its template's materials by slot; numbers the server
  wouldn't draw leave the template's mesh, so a project still opens. Its selection box, its physical box and a
  pasted copy follow the drawn wall.

  the solid's, one file for the same numbers however spelt, the cache's size, malformed numbers refused); the EXP-67
  project on a test server: the custom wall drawn with its doorway, −184 to 184, clear of the twin, the donor's six
  materials, the project still saved, a pasted copy drawn the same; the viewer, node, release and repo suites.

### Custom walls, proof of concept F2 and F3: fracturing walls made from numbers, built into the map; EXP-67 prepared

The section's next two stages, offline, and the game run made ready for the user. A wall made from numbers is a
copy of one of the map's fracturing walls (the donor) with a new mesh and new fragment columns; everything else
(materials, toughness, rubble, effects) is the donor's.
- [tools/bake/frac_wall.py](tools/bake/frac_wall.py) (new): the generator. A wall's numbers (its ends, its openings,
  a seed) give its mesh built as URB_Bar's inside wall `URB_BarIntWallB_FRACTURED` is: the six slots (each side's
  face by storey, the trims, the inside faces), the donor's cross-section with its skirting and cornice, its texture
  repeats and vertex colours, Voronoi fragments through the thickness (openings cut first) with their inside faces,
  records and neighbours, lightmap coordinates packed in the square, and one collision box for each solid round the
  openings. The same numbers always give the same mesh and name.
- [tools/bake/frac_walls.py](tools/bake/frac_walls.py) (new): in the map. A fracturing copy that carries
  `generated` (`fracWall` with the wall's numbers, or `relit`: the donor's own mesh lit as a made wall is, for a
  reference beside one) gets the mesh and its body setup under the package `XComMapEdGeo`, the component's
  `FragmentBoundsMinZ`, `FragmentBoundsMaxZ` and `NumResourceIndices` as the game's walls save them, one painted
  colour for each new vertex, and its `FragmentColumns` by the audit's box rule.
- [native_copy.py](tools/bake/native_copy.py): such copies are made after the fracturing copies, their tiles seeded
  and rebuilt over the made wall's own box; the manifest lists them (`generatedWalls`), the log has a line for each,
  and the relight lights each from nothing. [relight.py](tools/bake/relight.py): `--fresh-copy COPY`, a new actor of
  the map lit from nothing as a foreign copy is.
- [compiler.py](tools/editor/compiler.py): an added copy's `generated` is checked (malformed, or on anything but a
  fracturing piece's copy: the record is left out), the copy stands in the made wall's box (`world_box`'s `along`),
  and the request goes through the spec and `native_split` to the Build; a note says a blast doesn't spread from a
  made wall to the walls beside it, nor from them to it. [web/app.js](tools/viewer/web/app.js) keeps a copy's
  `generated` through load, save and paste (the view draws the template's mesh).
- [examples/exp67_project.py](tools/editor/examples/exp67_project.py) (new): EXP-67's project on URB_Bar (a reference,
  the twin, a custom wall four tiles long with a doorway), saved in the editor's store and built there, or in a
  scratch folder. [EXP-67](research/experiments/EXP-67-fracturing-wall-poc.md) with

### The output-name check no longer takes the lab's earlier tests of a project for someone else's files

The user's queued build of temple_improved failed at once: "the build would write names that are taken:
patch_templeship_templeim_2001", a file the lab's patchtool had put in the lab copy on 7 November for that same
project, and one the build would not even write. 24 projects were refused the same way by their own earlier tests'
files ([findings register](research/findings-register.md) T-40).
- [build.py](tools/editor/build.py) `output_names`: the patch's name is checked only when the edit makes a patch (the
  compile has said so by then; the check as the package goes in already went by the manifest).
- [installs.py](tools/viewer/installs.py) `lab_deploys`: in the lab copy (its `XComLab-copy.txt` marker) with the lab
  setting set, the files the lab's deploy tools put there (the bake fixtures' `deployed.json` with each hash,
  patchtool's `deployed.txt` and `seeded.txt`, as `deploy_fixture.patchtool_owns` reads them). `preflight` lets an
  install replace such a file of the package's own names if it still has the bytes the lab gave it; `_copy_files`
  keeps it in that change's backup folder first (`labFiles` in `installs.json`), and `_files_out` puts it back when
  the editor's file comes out (a play's end, Remove from game). Any other install, or no lab, is as before.
- [outputnames.py](tools/viewer/outputnames.py) `Claims`: such a file is a soft claim, so it no longer stops the
  project's build and still keeps a new project from taking the name.
- [viewer README](tools/viewer/README.md): the install paragraph said any file of a package's names is replaced, which
  it hasn't been since Output names N1; it now gives the rule and the lab's exception.
- [EXP-65](research/experiments/EXP-65-build-queue-real-builds.md) gets a correction: its first refusal (and the Q4
  entry below, "the snapshot builds keep their name checks") was this fault, not the check working.

### Build queue Q1: the queue on the server, kept across restarts

[buildqueue.py](tools/viewer/buildqueue.py), new (private build queue plan, stage Q1): projects queued for full
builds, built one after another by one worker, each captured as saved when its turn comes into an immutable snapshot
(`<builds>/.work/queue-attempts/<attempt>/project.json`) and built with every folder pinned from the queue's context.
Its package is verified as that attempt's (token, project, revision, full build, files) before the row is built. A
project that can't be read or doesn't build fails alone; a store that can't be written holds the queue and says so.
The queue reserves the build slot while it runs, waits for a build already running and for readers of the next
project's package, and lets go of the slot in the same step that stops or finishes it. Stop closes dispatch at once
and stops only its own build (a row whose package went in first stays built); Resume captures again. Rows can be
removed while waiting; Clear removes rows and results, never projects or packages.

The queue is `<builds>/.work/build-queue.json` (unique temporary file, replace, last good copy as `.bak`), owned by
one server through an OS-held lock on `build-queue.lock` taken once the port is bound. A restarted server starts
nothing: rows left starting or building wait until an earlier server's build of them is proved gone, then become
built if that attempt's package is in place (even without its result written) or wait again, and the queue is
stopped. A file it can't read, or of a newer schema, is kept and reported, never taken for an empty queue; a torn file
falls back to the last good copy, and `reset` sets it aside. Requests carry `{queueId, expectedRevision, requestId}`;
receipts (seven days, across Clear) answer a repeated request as the first time, even after a restart.

Routes in [viewer.py](tools/viewer/viewer.py): `GET /manager/queue.json` (no-store), `POST /manager/queue` (add),
`/stop`, `/resume`, `/remove`, `/clear`, `/reset`; `build-cancel` takes `{"attempt"}` and stops the queue for a queue's
build. A closing server stops its queue. [gamesetup.py](tools/viewer/gamesetup.py) refuses another game install while
the queue runs, before anything is saved; a stopped queue whose context changed can't resume or take rows.
[builds.py](tools/viewer/builds.py): `recovered_alive`.

Checked: [test_buildqueue.py](tools/viewer/tests/test_buildqueue.py), new, 22 tests with test_builds.py's stand-in
and event hooks (no timed sleeps for ordering): order and saves while waiting, failures apart, waits for another
build and for a reader, the slot held between rows, Stop while capturing (nothing launched), while building (Resume
builds the latest save as a new attempt), after the package went in, while waiting for another's build, Cancel from
the build window, a late ending, Add/Remove/Clear and receipts, nine requests at once (one worker, one row each), a
storage fault, a restart mid-row, a result lost after its package went in, an earlier server's build still running,

times in a row without a failure; the whole viewer suite and the repo suite pass. Known gaps: no manager UI or editor
chip yet (Q2, Q3); readers don't take leases yet; no real build was queued.

### Build queue Q0: contained builds, journalled package swaps, attempts

The groundwork the build queue needs (private build queue plan, stage Q0); the queue itself is not built yet.

- [procs.py](tools/viewer/procs.py), new: every build the server starts is a contained process tree. On Windows it is
  created suspended, put in a Job Object of its own that kills its processes when its last handle closes, then
  resumed; a process that can't be put in its job is killed before it runs. Stopping a build kills the whole tree and
  waits until each process seen in it has ended (the job's count drops a moment before they have). A process is named
  by its id and creation time, never by an id alone.
- [publication.py](tools/viewer/publication.py), new: a package goes in with a journal (written before anything moves,
  committed before the old package is deleted), and `recover` settles one left by a build that died between its two
  renames: the new package kept when it is wholly in place and matches its manifest, else the old one put back. A
  journal it can't read blocks that variant's builds with the reason and deletes nothing. The variant's lock is now
  held by the operating system (a byte-range lock), released when its holder ends and never taken from a live holder
  because time passed; until now a lock file was taken over by its age.
- [build.py](tools/editor/build.py): the swap goes through publication.py, its backup in `.work/publish` (old work
  folders' pruning never reaches it). New options for the server's launches: `--attempt` (a UUID, written in the
  manifest and the build's id and work folder, so two builds in one second differ), `--projects` and `--check-game`
  (a build of a private snapshot keeps its name checks against the projects and the other install), `--saved-file`
  and `--pinned` (nothing read from the settings). Work-folder pruning reads the new names.
- [builds.py](tools/viewer/builds.py): each launch is an attempt with an origin (foreground, prefab, queue) fixed
  before it can be seen; it ends only after its processes are all gone and a journal it left is settled, even when
  its output can't be read. A leftover process holding the output pipe no longer keeps a build running: once build.py
  exits, leftovers get 15 s, then are killed. Cancel takes an optional attempt id (a stale cancel stops nothing).
  Records of running builds (`<builds>/.work/writers`) let a restarted server prove an earlier server's builds gone
  (or keep the slot busy, with the reason, until they are) and settle journals before anything builds
  ([viewer.py](tools/viewer/viewer.py) calls it once the port is bound). The slot can be reserved (the queue's), and
  readers can lease packages (Install, the map pack, Play: next stage). `stop_process` stays for the exporter and the
  precache.
- [projects.py](tools/viewer/projects.py): `capture`, the saved file's bytes and digest read under the store's lock.

Checked: the viewer suite (386, new [test_procs.py](tools/viewer/tests/test_procs.py): a stand-in server killed
outright takes its child and grandchild with it, a process that can't be contained never runs;
[test_publication.py](tools/viewer/tests/test_publication.py): a process killed after each step of the swap leaves a
whole package once settled; [test_builds.py](tools/viewer/tests/test_builds.py): its stand-in now writes a manifest of
its own attempt and swaps it in with the journal, and new tests cover two builds in one second, stale cancels, cancel
and leftovers draining the grandchild, a prefab test's build contained, a build dying between its renames, a launch

### Build queue plan: reviewed against the build, manager and prefab lifecycles

Revised the private build queue plan; the feature is not implemented. The review of
[builds.py](tools/viewer/builds.py), [build.py](tools/editor/build.py),
[manager.py](tools/viewer/manager.py), [prefab_tests.py](tools/viewer/prefab_tests.py) and the editor's build UI
adds immutable per-attempt inputs, preserved output-name checks, shared dispatch ownership, exact cancellation,
process-tree containment and recoverable package publication before the queue UI. It covers package-read races
with Zip/Install/Play, persistent request identity, corrupt state, configuration changes, two-tab discovery and
honest progress/estimates. Clear removes finished results as well as waiting rows; adding to a stopped queue
leaves it stopped; restart reconciles outcomes and requires Resume. Stages and fault-injection checks now follow
those dependencies. The plan remains in the ignored private plans folder, as repository policy requires.

Checked: the repository runner's focused viewer checks (`test_builds`: 6; `test_manager`: 9;
`test_prefab_tests`: 13), private-plan relative links and unchanged LF endings, and the repo suite. The first
manager run lacked the standard Windows PowerShell module path in its installer subprocesses; restoring that
path for the test process made all nine pass. Known gaps: this is a design review, not validation of an implemented
queue; the proposed concurrency, containment, crash-recovery, browser and real-build checks still need to run.

### Output names N3: a baked build's lighting file is `<Map>_Lighting.tfc`

Stage N3 of the output names plan (private). A build whose relight writes a texture cache names it after the map
(`URB_BarFix_Lighting.tfc`), no longer `Lighting_<n>` from a hash of the variant's name; quick builds and full builds
whose lighting stays unchanged still have none. Packages built before keep theirs until rebuilt.
- [lighting_fixture.py](tools/bake/lighting_fixture.py): `cache_fname` reads a cache name as the FName it is stored
  as: a plain name with number 0, or a name ending `_<n>` (no leading zero, in range) as `<Name>` numbered n + 1,
  which takes precedence; `parse_cache_name` needs the text in the map's table and still refuses a `.tfc` already
  beside the source map.
- [native_copy.py](tools/bake/native_copy.py): on a baked build the cache's name is added to the grown map's table
  (`Grower.name`) before the growing write, so the relight, reading the grown map afresh, can write it.
- [build.py](tools/editor/build.py): `cache_name` is `<Variant>_Lighting`; the relight-only branch reads a named copy
  of the map in the work folder (`named_base`: the growing writer with the name added, the texture caches read where
  the map's are), never the game install's file. Help and docstrings of [relight.py](tools/bake/relight.py) and the
  tools above say the new form.
- With it, a correction to N2: [projects.py](tools/viewer/projects.py) checks only that saved output names are
  package names, so an old project with names over 30 characters still saves (the compiler refuses to build it and
  says to use Save as).

Checked: the editor, viewer, bake and upk suites, with new tests: cache-name vectors (plain, numbered, leading zero,
range, bad names); a plain name refused before a growing write adds it; on a grown copy of URB_Bar a redirect writes
the plain name (number 0) and its `.tfc`, and the map's bytes from the first chunk differ only at the texture's cache
name and mip records; a real baked transplant (FreshLight) with `URB_BarFresh_Lighting` names it in every moved
texture, the others keep `Lighting`; native_copy's baked builds add the name (one with the real zero-write relight);
the Build's relight-only branch uses the named copy and leaves the install's map as it was; a package of before
rebuilt full, quick, full; a campaign install keeps the old `Lighting_<n>.tfc` noted until Remove everything. Known
gaps: the game itself has not read a plain-named cache yet (EXP-63, prepared: next section).

### Output names N1: a build or install never replaces another project's package or files

Stage N1 of the output names plan (private), which has to be in before map names lose their id piece. New
[outputnames.py](tools/viewer/outputnames.py) says who holds which names (`Claims`): other projects' output names in
the projects folder, every build in the builds folder (its folder and every name its manifest lists), the packages and
DefaultMaps.ini records of the game install the editor reads and the one it plays in, and what the editor installed
there; names compared regardless of case, a project's own claims left out only where a manifest or the ledger says
they are its own. It also holds the name conversion and allocation N2 uses.
- [build.py](tools/editor/build.py): the builds folder's package of the variant's name is replaced only when its
  manifest names the same project (`owned_folder`), checked before any tool runs; after the compile, every name the
  build may write (map, patch, texture cache, intro and stream copies) must be free for the project (`preflight`);
  both again as the package goes in, under a lock file in `<output>/.work/locks`, and a failed swap puts the old
  folder back. The command line checks the install Play in game uses too.
- [installs.py](tools/viewer/installs.py): Play in game's install and the project manager's campaign install check the
  whole package before anything is written (`preflight`): a variant installed for another project, a file in
  CookedPCConsole the editor didn't put there (any case), one installed for another project or for no known project,
  and one changed since are refused. The ledger notes whose each file is (`owners`); a ledger from before gives the
  files of the package's own list to the project it says installed the variant. The campaign install now plans and
  checks its config lines before copying files. One install at a time per server.
- [run_tests.py](tools/run_tests.py): the suites write UTF-8 and a console that can't show a character no longer
  stops the run (a message with curly quotes did).

Checked: the editor and viewer suites, with new tests: foreign, unreadable, case-only and missing-manifest build
folders refused with nothing run and nothing changed (the command line too); taken intro copy, cache and duplicate
project names refused, a quick build not stopped by a cache name; a failed swap leaves the last package; installs
refuse each foreign or changed file and leave config and files byte for byte; a project's own files replaced, an
identical file not the editor's used and left, an older ledger's ownership recovered or refused. Known gaps: two
servers on one projects folder or install are not kept apart (the lock file covers builds only).
